prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: دورات تدريبية معتمدة (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "اسم الدورة" · longest unbreakable word 67px · one-line width 250px
  col 2: header "المدة" · longest unbreakable word 50px · one-line width 168px
  col 3: header "المدرب" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 105px
  col 4: header "الوصف" · longest unbreakable word 73px · one-line width 1420px
  col 5: header "الرسوم" · longest unbreakable word 43px · one-line width 70px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A course-catalog comparison table: each row is one certified training course, and the reader picks a course by name, checks duration/trainer/fee, and reads the description only for shortlisted rows.","reading":"Right-to-left: the eye enters at the right on the course name (the row identity), then moves left across duration and fee for quick comparison, treating trainer and description as supporting detail. Scanning is vertical down the name column and horizontal only between duration and fee.","groups":["col 1 (اسم الدورة) is the row header and anchor for every other column","col 2 (المدة) and col 5 (الرسوم) are the two short quantitative comparators and should read as a pair","col 3 (المدرب) and col 4 (الوصف) are supporting detail, read only after a row is shortlisted"],"keep_intact":["الرسوم values (short numbers, 43px word)","المدرب names (55px words) — personal names must not split","duration units and parentheticals (أيام / ساعة / بواقع)","Latin tokens inside names: Excel, PMP"],"may_wrap":["الوصف (1420px one-line) — the only genuinely long text, absorbs wrapping into 3–6 lines","اسم الدورة (250px) can take 2 lines without breaking identity","المدة (168px) can wrap the parenthetical onto a second line"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[120,72,56,47,64],"idea":"Zero-scroll squeeze: everything fits 359px, name and duration wrap to 3–4 lines and the description collapses into a narrow tall strip that is effectively a keyword teaser rather than prose."},{"name":"B","widths":[230,140,95,180,70],"idea":"Compact horizontal scroll (~2 screens): course name, trainer and fee stay essentially one-line, duration wraps only its parenthetical, and the description gets a modest readable column."},{"name":"C","widths":[250,168,105,400,70],"idea":"Reading-optimized wide layout (~993px, scrolls): the four short columns sit at their natural one-line widths so names, durations, trainers and fees never break, and the description gets a genuine prose measure of 3–4 lines."}]}
